newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles County may face $433 mln gap - officials.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles County may face $433 mln gap - officials.

text.p: Los Angeles County could face a projected budget shortfall of $433 million for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, the county's chief administrative officer warned.

In a preliminary forecast, county Chief Administrative Officer David Janssen estimated that the general fund faced a $220 million gap while the county health department could be short $213 million in 1997-1998, which begins July 1.
"These numbers are fluid. These are rough estimates at this time," county spokeswoman Judy Hammond said Wednesday.
Janssen was expected to issue a fuller accounting of the county's budget position in January.

Janssen's figures assume that the county will not backfill any loss of revenues due to Proposition 218, a statewide measure approved by voters in November to limit the taxing authority of local governments. The county has decided to ask a judge to validate the county's assessment for fire services, Hammond said.
